title: Pairs for €4

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Account for indivisible promotional bundles and odd demand.

misconception: Two-for-one always halves the checkout cost for the exact quantity needed.
objective: Account for indivisible promotional bundles and odd demand.

claims.text: Singles cost €3 each. A two-for-one pair costs €4; pairs are indivisible. Scaled model; fictional offer; pair-only purchase.

claims.text: Title: Pairs for €4. You buy 3. You pay? Options: €6 / €8 / €12. Correct: €8.
claims.source: Prediction line from company/decisions/2026-10-15-lifehacks-r11-fix-plan.md (wave W7), implemented by demo-builder 2026-10-15; options and answer in src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json. One item: 1/2 rounded up = 1 pair = €4 (slider min 1). | FC pass 51 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15, W-1101): VERIFIED. Pairs-only: 3 items → 2 pairs → €8 (spec index 1); €6 is half the pair price per item, €12 is €4 per item. recall.question: Singles cost €3 each; a two-for-one pair costs €4 and pairs cannot be split. You need five items. What does the pairs-only checkout cost?
